title: News of the fish-bone war reaches Cathair mhòr
summary: A wool-merchant brings Eithne nic Ailein, last living of the nine who cut the cord at Roinn na Rìoghachd, the tale of Iain Garbh's war on Caol leathan. She does not ride to it and does not send to it, judging it another share's quarrel to end.

title: Word of the harbour wall at Caol fhiadhaich
summary: The wool-merchant's next journey brings word to Cathair mhòr of how Caol fhiadhaich fed besieged Caol leathan by night and was given a share of the western tolls, with which it raised the first stone wall that coast has had. Eithne asks after the wall every year after.

title: Iain Garbh never climbs to the cup
summary: Iain Garbh rules forty years past the end of Cogadh nan Rathad and never once goes up the mountain road to stand before the cup, unlike every rìgh before or after him. He dies unreconciled to the flame that had refused his warband its blessing.

title: Catrìona Ghlic crowned at Dùn dhearg
summary: Catrìona, daughter of Iain Garbh, is crowned at Dùn dhearg on her father's death and takes within ten years the name Catrìona Ghlic, Catrìona the Wise, for undoing the coldness he had left between the rìgh's hall and Talla na Lasrach.

title: The rìgh's tithe sent again to Talla na Lasrach
summary: Eithne nic Ailein, hearing that Catrìona Ghlic's son has sat a season with the flame unasked, orders that Cathair mhòr's own hall send its tithe to Talla na Lasrach's handful again, unwaited-for, as it had not done since her own father's day.

title: Coimheadaiche na Lasrach keeps a place for the rìgh's son
summary: After his first season carrying the baskets at Dùn ìseal, Catrìona Ghlic's son returns each year at the turn of the season, and Coimheadaiche na Lasrach comes to keep a place for him at the long table without being asked, a small thing the island reads as the breach mended.

title: Inis mhòr asks the crown for its own guard
summary: The wool port of Inis mhòr, grown past every other town in the north on the trade the two new waypoint houses carry, asks Catrìona Ghlic's crown for a road-guard of its own, and is given one without argument.

title: Niall Òg walks his last road
summary: Niall Òg comes on foot and unannounced to Eithne nic Ailein's hall at Cathair mhòr, the last road he means to walk, so that Oidhche an Dòrlaich should be told once more, to the only other living witness of it, before he dies.

title: Death of Niall Òg
summary: Niall Òg dies in his sleep by Eithne nic Ailein's own fire at Cathair mhòr, some two thousand years old, three days after telling her Oidhche an Dòrlaich for what proves the last time. She sends his body up the mountain at her own cost.

title: Niall Òg laid near the first heirs
summary: Eithne has Niall Òg laid near the old graves on the slope below Dùn ìseal, among the first heirs of Roinn na Rìoghachd, though he was of no kin to her own share, judging that a man who spent four hundred years walking every road on the island had earned the ground.

title: Eithne asks the count of her own years
summary: In her last year Eithne nic Ailein asks her steward more than once to reckon the exact tale of her days, wanting the number fixed precisely at the end, though her mind has not begun to fail her.

title: Eithne's hall at Cathair mhòr falls silent
summary: With Eithne nic Ailein's death her hall at Cathair mhòr is left to her stewards and her reciters, who keep the rolls but crown no one there, the lowland share having long since ceased to answer to any single hand of her line.
